summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents over the last quarter, and alignment on a short pilot for Dedicated capacity. Customer is seeing increased token volume, wants to reduce tail latency for interactive workflows and get more predictable unit cost. Security team requested SOC2 docs, SAML/SSO details, and KMS encryption flow. Team agreed to run a 1-week pilot benchmark and review pricing for Dedicated vs hosted plus autoscale burst options.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-14 16:00 UTC; Duration: 45m; Attendees: Lena Ortiz, Miguel Santos, Priya Kapoor (Redwood) / Sarah Blake, Tom Ruiz, Aisha Khan, David Lee (Northpoint)

00:00 - Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Lena from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, Miguel our SE is here, Priya from CSM as well. How's everyone's day?
00:08 - Sarah Blake: Morning, yeah all good. Wanted to use the QBR to walk through where we're at with usage, some reliability stuff, and talk about the Dedicated option you mentioned last month.
00:18 - Miguel Santos: Great. Quick agenda — usage/costs, incidents, roadmap + pilot options. We'll leave time for security Qs at the end. Does that work?
00:24 - Tom Ruiz: Yep.
00:29 - Sarah Blake: Quick context — we've ramped up conversational routing for our driver support product, token volumes up ~3x q/q, latency has crept up during peak. We're hitting p95 around 420ms and p99 spikes to 1.1s occasionally.
00:45 - Miguel Santos: Thanks. We looked at your telemetry — the prefix cache hit rate is around 18% for the support flows, and batching is limited by variable request sizes. That's increasing per-token cost. Dedicated pools with a tighter quantization profile and optimized batching could cut unit cost 25-40% depending on traffic patterns.
01:02 - David Lee: When you say quantization profile, are we talking 4-bit? We tried a q4 path and saw some semantic drift on summarization.
01:10 - Miguel Santos: Right, 4-bit can sometimes change output fidelity on some prompts. Our recommendation is a staged approach: start with q8 or mixed-precision for the pilot, run evals on your prompt set, compare against hosted baseline.
01:22 - Aisha Khan: From security, we need SOC2 docs, and we need to understand KMS flow — where keys live, HSM usage, and audit logs retention. Also SAML SSO for console access.
01:32 - Priya Kapoor: Absolutely, we can share the security pack and the network diagram. We support customer-managed KMS and have options for HSM integrations; audit logs are available with retention addons. I'll attach docs after the call.
01:45 - Sarah Blake: Cool. On reliability, we had two incidents last month where a regional autoscaler misrouted to a lower tier model variant and latency spiked. Can you recap fallback behavior?
01:56 - Miguel Santos: Sure, the smart routing policy falls back to compatible model variants but respects latency SLOs; however if capacity is constrained and burst rules trigger, you can configure automatic fallbacks or failover to another region. We saw in your traces that fallback occurred but the variant had different latency characteristics. For the pilot we suggest pinning model versions and enabling canary rollout to verify performance.
02:18 - Tom Ruiz: For the pilot benchmark, what metrics do you need from us? We want to validate throughput (qps), per-token cost, and tail latency under production load.
02:27 - Miguel Santos: We'll need a representative prompt corpus, target concurrency profile, and a set of success criteria. Our perf tests will measure p50/p95/p99, throughput sustained for 30m windows, and token cost estimates with and without prefix caching.
02:40 - Sarah Blake: We can share a 2k prompt sample and a production traffic replay for a 1-week pilot window.
02:47 - Miguel Santos: Perfect. We'll draft the benchmark plan and share next week.
02:53 - David Lee: Pricing — your hosted costs have risen. We need committed pricing for Dedicated but also want burst capacity for irregular spikes.
03:02 - Lena Ortiz: We have reserved-capacity pricing tiers and burst add-ons. For the pilot we'll provide a blended estimate and a path to commit after the benchmark. I'll send a short spreadsheet showing unit economics (hosted vs dedicated) and expected savings at different QPS.
03:17 - Aisha Khan: Also curious about data residency: some driver data needs to stay in the EU region for GDPR reasons. Do you support region pinning?
03:27 - Miguel Santos: Yes, region pinning is supported. Private deployments or Dedicated regional pools can ensure data stays in-region; we can also discuss VPC endpoints for Private mode if you need more controls.
03:40 - Sarah Blake: Any competitors you see customers using for similar setups?
03:44 - Lena Ortiz: We often see Anthropic and managed OpenAI endpoints in the market; some teams also prefer self-hosting with internal infra for cost control but then trade off engineering ops.
03:54 - Tom Ruiz: Noted.
03:58 - Miguel Santos: Quick note on reliability — enabling prefix caching and increasing min-batch size for those high concurrency windows will reduce cost and stabilize p95. We'll include config suggestions in the pilot plan.
04:10 - Sarah Blake: Sounds good. On success criteria: we'd like p95 under 350ms for interactive workflows and a 30% reduction in per-token cost compared to current hosted spend. Is that realistic?
04:22 - Miguel Santos: It's achievable with Dedicated + cache tuning; we'll quantify in the benchmark.
04:28 - Priya Kapoor: I'll set up the follow-up calendar invite for the pilot kickoff and include the security pack and pricing spreadsheet.
04:35 - Lena Ortiz: Recap of next steps — Lena to send pricing spreadsheet, Miguel to draft benchmark and perf tests, Aisha to share KMS and network topology, Sarah to confirm dataset and criteria. We'll schedule pilot for week of 4/27 pending confirmation.
04:54 - Sarah Blake: Thanks everyone.
05:00 - Lena Ortiz: Thanks, we'll follow up by Friday.

(Transcript notes: automated transcription had low confidence on some product names (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cache" in places), occasional speaker mislabels, some timestamps approximate.)
